Republic Of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: Ilwww.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 09 s. 2023 FEB 22 2023 DIR. WILHELM M. SUYKO Regional Director, DILG-Region X KM3 Fr. W.F. Masterson Avenue Upper Carmen, Cagayan de Oro City Misamis Oriental Dear RD suyko: This pertains to your earlier communication regarding the complaints filed by concerned citizens of Misamis Occidental and Camiguin, regarding various policies of the local government units (LGUs) barring them from availing of certain services unless they have received their vaccines and booster shots. Particularly, among the fifteen (15) complaints, eight (8) referred to a "No Vaccine/Booster, No Pension/Ayuda" Policy, five (5) referred to a "No Vaccine/Booster, No Transaction Policy", and. one (1) "No Vaccine/Booster, No Travel/Entry" Policy all from the Province of Misamis Occidental. One (1) complaint from the Province of Camiguin referred to a "No Vaccine/Booster, No Entry/Travel" Policy being implemented as well. Consequently, when the local chief executives were asked for comments, they cited the provisions of Executive Order No. HSO-016 s. of 2022 which was issued by the Provincial Government of Misamis Occidental, as their legal justification or basis for implementing such policies, specifically Sections 3 and 5 thereof which states: "Section 3. OPERATION OF ESTABLISHMENTS AND MASS GATHERINGS. All establishments, or activities are allowed to operate or be undertaken full on-site or venue/seating capacity provided that all individuals, employees, and customers shall present proof of vaccination with booster doses (i.e. vaccination cards, vaccination certificates, etc.) before entry into establishments or before participating in mass gatherings. SECTION 5. NON-COMPLIANCE. Non-compliance of the aforesaid vaccination program shall obligate the said person to present a negative RT-PCR test result, with a validity of sevety- two (72) hours, every fifteen (15) days before entry into workplaces, establishments, industries, academes, etc. " Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54 CamScanner

Under this premise arose your request for guidance and legal opinion regarding the propriety of the measures imposed by these LGUs, as well as recommendations on the legally appropriate course of action of the Regional Office. At the outset, it is indisputable that the coronavirus has greatly caused and is continuing to cause loss of lives and disruption to the economy. Correspondingly, it cannot be gainsaid that all efforts, which are within the bounds of the law, must be exerted in order to prevent or at least limit the spread of the coronavirus, as well as to address the socio-economic devastation brought about by this pandemic. However, we deem it proper to emphasize that there is no legal basis to deny nor disqualify unvaccinated individuals as beneficiaries to government cash assistance distribution, "ayuda", grants, or subsidies, as well as transacting with the government regarding essential services, as there is yet a law requiring mandatory vaccination. In addition, the issuances of the national governmentl, only provide that LGUs shall adopt measures to strictly implement and enforce the minimum public health standards set by the Department of Health (DOH) and other standards set by relevant government agencies2. Accordingly, the LGUs, instead, may encourage its respective inhabitants to get vaccinated by providing incentives in exchange for getting COVID-19 vaccine shots/boosters but, it cannot discriminate nor refuse to proceed in granting and/or processing the essential government-related transactions or services. In this regard, we are of the view that the issuance by the LGUs are discriminatory and oppressive to unvaccinated individuals. While at first glance, it would seem that the issuance by these LGUs are not requiring mandatory vaccinations, however, if we would delve into its provisions, unvaccinated individuals could be denied entry to receive their "ayuda" or proceed with their government-related transactions, unless they are vaccinated or except if they would be able to provide a negative RT-PCR test result for Covid-19 at their own expense. Therefore, in essence, it is actually a circumvention in order to require mandatory vaccination for all its inhabitants. Furthermore, while being vaccinated could lessen the chance of contracting the virus, however, it is also true that it does not guarantee that a vaccinated individual would not contract the COVID-19 virus anymore, bearing in mind that its primary purpose is not to prevent contracting the virus, but to be an added protection if case an individual becomes infected so that he/she would not suffer severe symptoms. Relatedly, individuals, whether vaccinated or unvaccinated, may be asymptomatic when they have the virus. Likewise, symptoms of the virus usually manifest only after a few days from contracting it, which means that an individual might already be a carrier without him/her knowing it unless there is continuous testing. Correspondingly, even vaccinated individuals may still contract the virus and may actually spread it. GUIDELINES ON THE NA TIONWIDE IMPLEMENTATION OF ALERT LEVEL SYSTEM FOR COVID-19 RESPONSE (As of June 04, 2022), as amended. 2 IA TF Resolution No. 169 (June 27, 2022), amending the provisions of IATF Resolution Nos. 149 in relation to 148-B. 2 CamScanner

In addition, vaccinated individuals also use the same transportation system such as jeeps, buses, trains, taxis, etc., and they also go to certain places to eat, or perform duties related to their work, wherein they are exposed to other individuals who may be unvaccinated. Most importantly, it would only cultivate and generate a false sense of security that being vaccinated alone would be enough to be protected from the virus. Similarly, as to the "No Vaccine/Booster, No Entry/Travel" policy, we would like to invite your attention to the Matrix of Entry, testing, and Quarantine Protocols for Incoming Travelers whether Filipino of Foreign Nationals (Pursuant to IATF Resolution No. 2), dated November 08, 2022 issued by the IATF, wherein it provides the protocols regarding easing travel restrictions for inbound travelers for fully vaccinated individuals and unvaccinated, partially vaccinated, or whose vaccination status cannot be independently validated. Therefore, the guidelines set forth therein shall' be strictly complied with by all LGUs in relation to inbound travelers. Hence, it is our stand that the subject issuances of the LGUs are unduly oppressive and discriminatory as the means employed is not reasonably necessary to attain the objective sought. In view of the foregoing, this Department would like to emphasize that while theLGUs enjoy local autonomy and are empowered to issue the necessary orders within their jurisdiction pursuant to the to the general welfare clause provided under Republic Act No. 7160 or known as the "Local Government Code of 1991", however, it must, at all times, make sure that such orders are in harmony and compliant with existing policies of the national task force and applicable protocols. Thus, orders and issuances passed by LGUs must adhere to the directives of the national government and if said orders or issuances were passed prior to the adoption of said policies, the LGU concerned should take the initiative in modifying/amending its directive to conform thereto. Consequently, the Provincial Government of Misamis Occidental is hereby enjoined to modify/amend Executive Order Nos. 26 and 28 to correspond with existing laws, policies of the national government and guidelines of the IATF Please be guided accordingly. Very truly yours, BY ORITY OF THE SECRETARY: AN CTOR R. LLAMAS Und r cretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELlAJVRL/LLLs-LRALLD/rjki 3 CamScanner
